text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- State overseas aid organisation Danida has not been able to reach the poorest among developing countries through the past 25 years, a report on the agency concludes.

--- State railway company DSB expects more Danes to go by train when the Great Belt fixed bridge and tunnel connection opens for train traffic in June this year. Estimates show that some one million more Danes than today will take the train within the first 12 months after the opening.
--- McDonalds has withdrawn its present national tv-campaign after 125 people have been food-poisoned from eating at McDonalds and is now destroying large quantities of beef and cheese.

--- Only a few months before the first train is to drive through the new fixed Great Belt bridge and tunnel connection, passengers safety in case of an accident is still uncertain. A very chaotic DSB life-saving drill on Wednesday did not live up to expectations at all, but it is doubtful whether DSB will have time for a new drill to correct mistakes.

--- 1200 employees throughout the country in Denmark's largest bank, Den Danske Bank, went on strike on Thursday, to protest against planned firings of 550 employees.More strikes could spread to other large banks in near future.
--- A new economics ministry report estimates that new wage rises of 6-7 percent within the next two years will not harm competitiveness.
